tasks.short: Check month-end records and statements in AFAS against subledgers, bank and agency invoices; fix errors before close.

steps.what: Export trial balance, subledgers and journal lists from AFAS
Tie out balances to bank, subledgers and agency invoices in Excel
Investigate breaks and unusual movements against last month and budget

loop.input: break list with linked journal lines, invoice texts and prior-month explanations
loop.output: proposed cause per break with the source lines cited
loop.check: every cited line must exist in AFAS and amounts must sum to the break; uncited claims are dropped
loop.stop: one pass per break, max 3 retries on failed check; otherwise marked 'needs accountant'
loop.why_not_simpler: causes sit in free-text journal descriptions and mails that rules cannot read

steps.what: Write close notes for the controller

loop.input: tie-out results and approved variance explanations
loop.check: all figures pulled by code, model writes text only; numbers in text compared to source
loop.stop: one draft, regenerate once on mismatch, else template with blanks
loop.why_not_simpler: narrative for the controller needs plain sentences per variance

tasks.design: Replace the monthly Excel tie-out workbook with a scheduled Python job on a governed data platform that pulls AFAS via its API, Rabobank CAMT.053 files and agency invoice data, reconciles every balance and posts a break list to a Power BI close dashboard. A bounded model step proposes causes for breaks and drafts the close memo; adjusting entries are prepared as AFAS import files that the accountant reviews and the controller approves before posting.
tasks.previous_blocker: Tie-outs depended on spreadsheet logic only the accountant knew, and building API pipelines for a 10-person finance team was too costly.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding makes small reconciliation jobs cheap to build and change; models can read journal descriptions and draft explanations with a citation check.
tasks.still_hard: Judging whether an accrual or adjustment is right, and multi-step reasoning across files, where models still fail often.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing the business behind a number (a site, a season of flex hiring, a disputed agency invoice) and signing off that the books are right.

ambition.what: Run the full tie-out weekly instead of only at month end, so breaks are fixed before close starts.

tasks.altitude: The accountant spends close days on breaks and judgement instead of copying figures; they decide which tie-outs and tolerances the job runs.

reach.learn: how variance explanations feed the forecast the business trusts
where agency invoice errors start, so rules catch them earlier

evidence.claim: AI beat licensed CPAs on month-end scenarios that reward detail and following instructions, vendor-run study
On broader accounting tasks top models meet about 62% of criteria; multi-step reasoning causes most errors
Firms using AI closed 7.5 days faster
Workday prepares entries for human review rather than posting them
Unnoticed model assumptions make workpapers impossible to rebuild

assumptions: AFAS Profit API (GetConnectors) access is available for ledger and subledger data
Rabobank statements can be exported as CAMT.053
Agency invoice data is available as files or portal export
unknowns: How many balance-sheet accounts are reconciled each month today
Whether the auditor accepts system-generated tie-outs as workpapers
Whether a governed data platform already exists or must be set up
research_questions: What share of close time is spent on breaks versus copying data, measured over two closes?
Can all three agency portals export invoice lines in a stable format?
Does the auditor accept automated reconciliations with an audit trail?

tasks.short: Review AFAS bookkeeping and procedures for errors, weak controls and inefficient ways of recording.

steps.what: Pull journals, user rights and supplier master changes from AFAS
Sample and test transactions in Excel for procedure breaches
Review exceptions and ask bookkeepers why they happened
Write findings and proposed procedure changes

loop.input: exception verdicts with counts and examples
loop.output: findings memo draft with proposed fixes
loop.check: counts and amounts inserted by code; accountant edits and signs
loop.stop: one draft per review cycle; fallback is the empty template
loop.why_not_simpler: findings need readable sentences tailored to each exception type

tasks.design: Replace Excel sampling with deterministic tests on the governed data platform that run over every AFAS transaction each month: duplicate invoices, segregation of duties, supplier IBAN changes, manual journals after close and late postings, shown on a Power BI control dashboard. The accountant reviews exceptions with the bookkeepers, and a bounded model step drafts the findings memo.
tasks.previous_blocker: Testing every transaction needed scripts nobody in finance could build or maintain, so the team sampled by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding makes full-population tests quick to write and adjust; AFAS data is reachable through its API.
tasks.still_hard: Deciding whether an exception is a real control failure or a valid business case, and getting people to change how they work.
tasks.human_edge: Talking with bookkeepers about why a rule was bypassed and judging whether the procedure or the person needs to change.

ambition.what: Check supplier IBAN changes and segregation of duties every week across all transactions instead of a yearly sample.

tasks.altitude: The accountant moves from sampling to deciding which controls run and what counts as an exception; fewer surprises in the audit.

reach.learn: which changes carry fraud risk and how to verify them
which control evidence the auditor relies on

evidence.claim: Internal control tests over every transaction suit deterministic software; interviews stay human
Model-written findings must stay traceable, since unnoticed assumptions break workpapers

assumptions: AFAS logs supplier master changes and user rights in exportable form
Bookkeepers are available for exception follow-up
unknowns: Whether the works council sees per-user control tests as monitoring of staff that needs consent
Which controls the external auditor currently tests
How many supplier IBAN changes happen per month
research_questions: How many exceptions does a full-population test produce per month, and how many are real?
Can AFAS expose the authorisation and change logs through the API?
Does the works council require consent under the WOR for tests that name individual users?

tasks.short: Direct bookkeepers in filing, recording and sending financial records; track the close checklist and deliveries.

steps.what: Assign and track close tasks with an Excel checklist and mail
Chase missing documents such as agency invoices and statements
Check that records are posted and filed with support
Compile and send records to the auditor and tax office

tasks.design: Move the Excel close checklist into a SharePoint list or Planner board with due dates and Teams reminders, and add a scheduled job that checks AFAS for posted journals, attached invoices and expected agency invoices and statements, feeding a completeness dashboard. Auditor packs are assembled by code from the request list; the accountant checks and sends them.
tasks.previous_blocker: The checklist lived in one spreadsheet and completeness checks meant opening records one by one.
tasks.enabler_now: Microsoft 365 lists and Power Automate are already licensed; AI coding makes the AFAS completeness checks cheap to build.
tasks.still_hard: Records arriving late from agencies and judging what an auditor or the tax office actually needs.
tasks.human_edge: Leading the bookkeepers, spotting why someone keeps making the same mistake, and owning what leaves the company.

ambition.what: A live close status page the Finance Director and controller can open any day of the close.

tasks.altitude: Less chasing by mail; the accountant decides priorities when the dashboard shows delays and spends time coaching.

reach.learn: which missing attachments block the close most often
which step drives days to close

evidence.claim: Recordkeeping and directing filing staff suits a copilot with low autonomy
Large companies must file accounts with KVK via SBR from FY2025; AFAS cannot file this for them

assumptions: Microsoft 365 licences include Lists, Planner and Power Automate
Invoice documents are attached in AFAS rather than kept only in mailboxes
unknowns: How the KVK SBR filing is done today and by whom
Which documents the auditor requests each year
How many agency invoices arrive late per month
research_questions: How many hours per close go to chasing documents by mail?
Can AFAS report invoices without an attached document through the API?
Would the bookkeepers use a shared task list instead of mail?

tasks.short: Change and document AFAS setup, ledgers, VAT codes and finance tools, and keep procedures current.

steps.what: Collect change needs such as new cost centres, sites or VAT codes
Configure AFAS ledger, VAT codes, allocations and workflows
Build Excel and Power BI links between AFAS and other sources
Document procedures and setup in SharePoint

loop.input: change specification, configuration diff and test result
loop.check: accountant reviews; screen names and codes checked against the AFAS export
loop.stop: one draft per change; fallback is manual writing
loop.why_not_simpler: procedures are prose for bookkeepers and change with every setup change

tasks.design: Keep AFAS as the system of record and configure it directly; replace ad-hoc Excel links with small, version-controlled Python jobs on the governed data platform, written with AI coding help, with tie-out tests rerun after every change. A bounded model step drafts procedure updates from the change specification and configuration diff for the accountant to check.
tasks.previous_blocker: Finance could not write or maintain code, so links lived in fragile spreadsheets and documentation lagged behind changes.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding lets an accountant specify and review small jobs and tests; reusable tie-out tests make regression checks cheap.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing the right ledger and VAT design, preparing for Dutch e-invoicing whose rules are not yet law, and AFAS configuration that stays screen work.
tasks.human_edge: Designing the chart of accounts and VAT setup so it fits the CAO, the sites and the auditor, and getting the controller's agreement.

ambition.what: An e-invoicing readiness plan for AFAS ahead of the planned 2030 B2B obligation.

tasks.altitude: The accountant specifies and reviews systems instead of hand-building spreadsheets, and owns the test set that every change must pass.

reach.learn: how the nightly extract is built and governed
which ledger structure makes forecasting easier

evidence.claim: Dutch B2B e-invoicing planned from 1 July 2030, not law yet
Intra-EU and reverse-charge invoice timing rules are changing under ViDA
No benchmark covers Dutch GAAP or Dutch VAT

assumptions: A test environment for AFAS Profit is available
Finance is allowed to run code on a governed platform managed with IT
unknowns: Whether IT allows finance-owned jobs on a shared data platform
How often AFAS setup changes per year
Who maintains the current Excel links
research_questions: How many Excel files link AFAS to other sources today, and which break most?
Can the accountant review AI-written jobs well enough with tests and a short training?
Which AFAS changes are needed for e-invoicing via Peppol?

role.altitude: From building tie-outs, samples and checklists by hand to setting the rules, tests and tolerances that check every entry, and spending the time saved on breaks, judgement and coaching bookkeepers.
reach: Work with FP&A on variance explanations that feed the forecast
Work with the controller on audit evidence and control design
Guide bookkeepers on where invoice and filing errors start
Prepare AFAS for Dutch e-invoicing and ViDA changes
skills_to_grow: Specifying and reviewing small data jobs and tests
Control design over full transaction populations
Reviewing model-drafted text against source figures
role.ambitious_version: A weekly soft close: every balance tied out and every control tested each week, so month end becomes a short check and days to close drops sharply.
